comparison: Both strongly support the primary convergence finding in the dysgranular mid-insula (C9-C10, C74-C75, C125-C127). OpenEval emphasizes anatomical specificity using cytoarchitectonic atlases, while peer reviewers explicitly affirmed this as 'compelling evidence.' Peer review also includes interpretive claims C16-C17 which OpenEval addresses separately in R13.

Perfect agreement on group differences and hemispheric asymmetry (C11-C13, C76, C79-C80, C128-C129). Both evaluations support these findings with OpenEval noting the connection to prior meta-analyses while acknowledging speculative mechanistic interpretation. Peer reviewers consistently affirmed the lateralization effect and its clinical significance.

Complete agreement on divergence analysis findings (C14, C96, C100, C105-C110, C132-C134). Both support the anterior agranular insula activation during uncertainty periods. OpenEval notes the unexpected lack of correlation with anxiety sensitivity (C111), which peer reviewers did not specifically challenge.

Full agreement on hemispheric dominance and correlation findings (C81-C84). Both evaluations support these results. OpenEval raises questions about the lack of correlation with objective physiological measures, while peer reviewers accepted these findings without challenge as supporting evidence for main conclusions.

Complete agreement on behavioral findings (C118-C124). Both support the dissociation between real-time and retrospective ratings and the VIA task findings. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these results as part of clinical characterization, while OpenEval explicitly notes the modality-specific differences.

Strong agreement on physiological and perceptual responses (C112-C117). Both support these findings. OpenEval emphasizes the dissociation between objective and subjective responses. Peer review includes C130 (interpretive claim) and notes Reviewer 3 requested clarification about saline differences, indicating acceptance with interest in interpretation.

Both evaluate connectivity findings (C90-C93) with uncertainty. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of temporal control condition limiting interpretation of task-specificity. Peer Reviewer 1 similarly raised concerns about whether findings represent 'fluctuations over time rather than following interoception specifically,' recommending future test-retest reliability studies.

Both support the theoretical background and knowledge gap (C1-C3, C59). OpenEval affirms these are well-supported by citations. Peer reviewers praised the theory-driven approach, with Reviewer 1 noting the study 'directly testing results from influential theories' and fills an important gap. Peer review also includes study design claims C61-C63.

Both address sample characteristics (C64-C73) but with different emphases. OpenEval supports the statistical documentation while noting medication use and comorbidity as potential unaddressed confounds. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about generalizability due to predominantly female sample, medication use, and fixed task order. Peer review also includes study design claims C4-C8, C60.

Partial overlap on study design claims (C4-C8, C60). OpenEval R2 supports the methodological rigor including preregistration and propensity matching. Peer R8 rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns about sample composition (gender imbalance, medication) and fixed task order, which OpenEval addresses separately in R3 regarding sample characteristics.

Both support null findings (C85-C89) as valid results. OpenEval notes these raise questions about functional significance and the lack of trait measure associations. Peer reviewers accepted these null results without challenge, viewing them as supporting the specificity of main findings regarding right dysgranular activation.

Both support the null finding regarding anxiety sensitivity correlation (C111). OpenEval finds this surprising given theoretical links between uncertainty and anxiety. Peer reviewers accepted this as part of comprehensive analysis showing specificity of correlations with real-time perception but not other measures.

Divergent evaluations of interpretive conclusions (C16-C18, C130-C131). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting that while convergence is well-supported, characterization as 'locus of disruption' is speculative based on correlational evidence. Peer reviewers included C16-C17 in their SUPPORTED evaluation of the convergence finding, with the editor calling it 'compelling evidence' for dysgranular insular involvement.

OpenEval evaluated connectivity findings C94-C95 (correlations with clinical measures) as UNCERTAIN due to unclear directionality and mechanism. These specific claims were not separately evaluated by peer reviewers, though C94-C95 appear in peer R9's list of accepted null findings.

Minor overlap on study design claims (C61-C63). OpenEval R2 supports the preregistration and experimental manipulations as part of overall methodological rigor. Peer R10 supports the theory-driven approach and pre-registered hypotheses as filling an important gap in the field.
